// Package fixture is a test fixture: the SAME job as ref_dec.c.txt (read
// quantised spectral lines band by band, then smooth them against the previous
// frame), written from the description of the job and not from the C. It is the
// CONTROL: copycheck must stay quiet on it.
package fixture

import "errors"

var errFrame = errors.New("frame longer than the transform")

// bandWidths are the widths of the scale-factor bands, in lines. They are
// derived here from a growth rule instead of listed.
func bandWidths(n int) []int {
	w := make([]int, 0, n)
	width := 4
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		w = append(w, width)
		if i >= 7 && i%2 == 1 {
			width += width / 3
		}
	}
	return w
}

type bitSource interface {
	Bits(n int) uint32
}

type spectrum struct {
	lines    []float64
	previous []float64
	budget   int
}

// escaped reads a magnitude whose prefix said "does not fit in three bits".
func escaped(src bitSource) (value, used int) {
	extra := 4
	used = 1
	for extra < 12 && src.Bits(1) == 1 {
		extra++
		used++
	}
	return 1<<extra | int(src.Bits(extra)), used + extra
}

func (s *spectrum) read(src bitSource, gains []float64, frame int) (int, error) {
	if frame > len(s.lines) {
		return 0, errFrame
	}
	consumed := 0
	pos := 0
	for band, width := range bandWidths(len(gains)) {
		for i := 0; i < width && pos < frame; i++ {
			prefix := int(src.Bits(3))
			consumed += 3
			magnitude := prefix
			if prefix == 7 {
				v, n := escaped(src)
				magnitude, consumed = v, consumed+n
			}
			v := float64(magnitude) * gains[band]
			if magnitude > 0 && src.Bits(1) == 1 {
				v = -v
				consumed++
			} else if magnitude > 0 {
				consumed++
			}
			s.lines[pos] = v
			pos++
		}
	}
	blend := 0.5
	for i := range s.lines[:frame] {
		s.lines[i] = blend*s.lines[i] + (1-blend)*s.previous[i]
	}
	copy(s.previous, s.lines)
	s.budget = min(s.budget+consumed, 6144)
	return consumed, nil
}
